svg.data-power-max-scope: 45 C ambient, optics fully populated, 100% traffic load (HIG); 894 W on the DC version and 890 W on the AC version
svg.data-psu-ac-input: 100-240 VAC, 12 A max; 16 A fast-acting fuse in the PSU
svg.data-psu-dc-input: -40 to -75 VDC, 40 A max; 60 A fast-acting fuse in the PSU
svg.data-fans: 4 hot-swappable modules, 3+1 redundant, exhaust; front-to-back airflow
svg.data-altitude: rated for operation up to 5000 m (HIG, Connecting Power)
svg.data-breakout: ports 0/1-0/4 are 25G SFP28 in-band ports sharing 100GE port 0
svg.data-coherent: the four QSFP-DD ports support 400G ZR and OpenZR+ transceivers
svg.data-timing: Stratum 3E OCXO with optional holdover, ITU-T SyncE, IEEE 1588v2 (G.8265.1 default, G.8275.1, G.8275.2, SMPTE ST 2059-2 with an additional licence), T-GM, T-BC/OC, T-TC, Class C accuracy, TSN
svg.data-timing-interfaces: GNSS SMA in, 10MHz SMB in/out, 1PPS SMB in/out, ToD RJ45 in/out
svg.data-timing-caveat: NOS integration is necessary to activate the specific feature (datasheet footnote)
svg.data-gnss: internal receiver for master clock; edge Grandmaster with PRTC, distributing phase and time via PTP G.8275.1
svg.data-optics-qsfp-dd: 400G QSFP-DD SR, LR, ER, ZR, OpenZR+
svg.data-optics-sfp28: 25G SFP28 SR, LR, ER; 10G SFP+ SR, LR, ER; 1G SFP SX, LX, EX
svg.data-console: RJ45 serial and micro-USB, 115200 8N1, no flow control; the micro-USB console needs a Silicon Labs CP210x USB-to-UART driver
svg.data-emc: FCC Part 15 Subpart B Class A; ICES-003 Class A; EN 55032 Class A; EN 55035; EN 300 386; EN 301 489; EN 303 413; EN 62479; EN 50663

This is the bare working chassis - the traffic cages ship empty.","kind":"base"},"dc-populated":{"airflow":"front-to-back","component-attrs":{"fan-803816-hi":{"model":"FAN-803816-HI"},"psu-132-dc":{"airflow":"exhaust","model":"PSU-132-DESR"}},"description":"The DC build with 25G optics fitted in the four SFP28 breakout ports","kind":"example","occupants":{"port-0-1":"common/sfp-lc-duplex@1","port-0-2":"common/sfp-lc-duplex@1","port-0-3":"common/sfp-lc-duplex@1","port-0-4":"common/sfp-lc-duplex@1"}}},"datasheet":{"title":"UfiSpace S9600-28DX 100G/400G Open Aggregation Router Datasheet","url":"https://www.ufispace.com/products/telco/aggregation/s9600-28dx-100g-400g-open-aggregation-router"},"description":"UfiSpace S9600-28DX 100G/400G Open Aggregation Router - 2RU, 24x QSFP28 100G + 4x QSFP-DD 400G (ZR/ZR+ capable) + 4x SFP28 25G breakout sharing 100G port 0, full timing (GNSS/1PPS/10MHz/ToD), Stratum 3E OCXO, SRv6, dual 1300 W PSUs and four hot-swap fans at the rear, front-to-back airflow","format":1,"gaps":[{"note":"This chassis orders PSU-132-DESR and PSU-132-AESR, both stated 'exhaust air flow' in the datasheet's Power Supply Types list. The components seated here, ufispace/psu-132-dc and psu-132-ac, were drawn for the S9300-32D and carry that device's intake-flow siblings PSU-132-DISB1 / PSU-132-AISB1 in `attrs.model` and `airflow: intake`. Both are overridden per configuration so this device reads correctly, but the contracts still describe the intake parts, and nothing in the intake shows a DESR or AESR face: whether the exhaust variants differ visually (the S9300-32D HIG says latch colour distinguishes airflow - red for front-to-back, blue for back-to-front) is unresolved, and this chassis's own rear figure draws a RED latch on a module the ordering line calls exhaust. Either the colour convention differs between families or one of the two documents is loose.","reason":"needs-hardware","scope":["psu-0","psu-1"],"wanted":"a photograph or drawing of a PSU-132-AESR/DESR face, or a UfiSpace PSU-132 datasheet covering all four suffixes","what":"psu-variant-attrs"},{"note":"HIG section 10 tables the six system lamps (SYNC, SYS, FAN, PS0, PS1, ID), the PSU FRU lamp and the Fan FRU lamp, and gives no table at all for the port lamps. The twenty-four four-lamp clusters on the two PCB strips, the two blue QSFP-DD light pipes and the arrows over the SFP28 block therefore keep their components' default of off/on rather than an invented link/activity vocabulary. Whether each cluster's four dots are four lanes or something else is not stated anywhere, which is the same silence ufispace/lane-led-quad records on its own contract.","reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["qsfp28","qsfpdd-400g","sfp28-breakout","port-leds"],"wanted":"a per-NOS LED table from UfiSpace or a NOS vendor, or photographs of a live unit with ports in known states","what":"port-led-semantics"},{"note":"The management RJ45 carries two green lamps at its bottom corners, plainly drawn in HIG Figure 8. Unlike the S9501-28SMT and M3000-14XC guides, this HIG's section 10 has NO 'Management port LED' table - it stops after the Fan FRU LED. So the two lamps are placed where the figure puts them and keep the component default rather than borrowing the sibling devices' left-green-1G / right-amber-100M vocabulary, which would be an assumption dressed as a citation. Note also that both lamps are drawn GREEN here where the siblings draw one green and one amber.","reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["mgmt"],"wanted":"this family's management port LED table, or a photograph of a linked unit","what":"management-jack-led-semantics"},{"note":"The datasheet says the four SFP28 ports are 'In-band port share with 100GE Port 0' and the HIG's overview calls the same thing '25G (through breakout cable)'. The faceplate agrees, colouring the lamp strip yellow and orange across exactly the SFP28 block and the port-0 column. What is NOT stated is the electrical rule: whether fitting the SFP28 ports disables port 0, whether they are a fixed 4x25G breakout of it, or whether they are separately switched. The model draws them as their own group and records the shared relationship in the group description and in attrs; it does not assert a rule the vendor has not written.","reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["sfp28-breakout","port-0"],"wanted":"a UfiSpace port-mapping note or a NOS interface listing from a live unit","what":"sfp28-breakout-relationship"},{"note":"No figure or photograph in the intake shows the underside, and the flanks appear only in the rack-mounting perspectives. The HIG states the flank hardware in words - five key-shaped attachment pins per side plus one M4 inner-rail screw - so the count and the kind are sourced and only the spacing is estimated. The underside carries only the house compliance sticker at an estimated position.","reason":"needs-photo","scope":["left","right","bottom"],"wanted":"straight-on photographs of a flank and of the underside","what":"side-and-underside-detail"}],"groups":{"fans":{"attrs":{"redundancy":"3+1","redundancy-note":"3+1 - hot swappable fan modules with 3+1 redundancy support (UfiSpace datasheet, staged intake)"},"description":"the vendor numbers the fans 0|1|2|3 in one legend on the rear panel","index-origin":0,"role":"service","term":"Fan"},"furniture":{"index-origin":1,"role":"furniture","term":"Item"},"grounding":{"index-origin":1,"role":"furniture","term":"Point"},"mgmt":{"index-origin":1,"mixed":"the management cluster - the RJ45 out-of-band jack, the USB 3.0 port, and two consoles that reach the same CLI (an RJ45 serial and a micro-USB), plus the recessed reset button","role":"management","term":"Port"},"port-leds":{"description":"every indicator that belongs to a particular port, ordered by that port","index-origin":1,"role":"indicator","term":"LED"},"psus":{"attrs":{"redundancy":"1+1","redundancy-note":"2x 1300 W 1+1 redundant, hot-swappable (exhaust airflow)"},"description":"the vendor spells the bays PSU0 and PSU1 on the rear panel","index-origin":0,"role":"service","term":"PSU"},"qsfp28":{"attrs":{"media":"qsfp28","speed":"100g"},"description":"ports 0-23, six columns of four - 40/100G, up to 80 km","index-origin":0,"role":"traffic","term":"Port"},"qsfpdd-400g":{"attrs":{"media":"qsfp-dd","speed":"400g"},"description":"ports 24-27, the 100/400G uplinks - up to 600 km with 400G ZR and OpenZR+ coherent optics","index-origin":0,"role":"traffic","term":"Port"},"sfp28-breakout":{"attrs":{"media":"sfp28","speed":"25g"},"description":"ports 0/1-0/4, the four 1/10/25G in-band ports that share 100GE port 0 through a breakout cable; the faceplate marks the shared group with a yellow and orange lamp band running across them and port 0","index-origin":1,"role":"traffic","term":"Port"},"status-leds":{"description":"the chassis indicators - SYNC, SYS, FAN, PS0, PS1, ID as printed on the white label strip beside them","index-origin":1,"role":"indicator","term":"LED"},"timing":{"index-origin":1,"mixed":"the timing column at the left-hand edge - a GNSS antenna on SMA, 1PPS and 10MHz on SMB and ToD on RJ45. Four media, one job, and no BITS on this platform","role":"management","term":"Port"}},"kind":"device","manufacturer":"UfiSpace","maturity":"modelled","model":"S9600-28DX","name":"s9600-28dx","portfolio":{"family":"Open Aggregation Router","line":"Telecoms","series":"S9600 Series"},"provenance":{"attrs":"datasheet (Specifications / Performance / Environmental / Regulatory Compliance / Accessories) and HIG (port overview for reach, section 11 for the console settings and the CP210x driver note). Compliance transcribed verbatim, not tidied - note the datasheet lists NOM and WEEE under Environment and carries no RoHS line, which is what it says. The datasheet writes 'IEEE 1558v2' in its feature bullets and 'IEEE 1588v2' in the specification table; the correct spelling is carried.","bottom":"estimated - no figure or photograph in the intake shows the underside. The compliance sticker is the house convention and its position is estimated. A bottom view mirrors LEFT and RIGHT, not front and back; the sticker is the only content and sits off-centre, so the mirror was applied rather than left to chance.","chassis":"datasheet - '2RU, 436 x 762 x 87.7 mm', 'Weight: 17.66kg or 38.93lb (without FRU)', repeated verbatim by the HIG's Component Physical Information table. The 436 mm is the BODY, not a rack face: the HIG's Space Clearance section says the width 'is 17.16 inches (43.6cm) and shipped with a rack mount brackets suitable for 19 inch (48.3cm) wide racks'. Ears are therefore not drawn - and note this chassis mounts on slide rails with five key-shaped attachment pins per flank, not on fixed brackets. Depth 762 is 'without the field replaceable units'; the HIG adds that the fan handles project 29 mm and the PSU handles 30 mm beyond it.","front-figure-scale":"drawing - GATE 1 PASSED CLEANLY ON BOTH AXES, which is rare in this intake. HIG Figure 8 (the port overview, extracted as fig-0015) draws the faceplate 1394 x 280 px for 436 x 87.7 mm: aspect 4.979 against a true 4.971, 0.16% out, i.e. 3.197 px/mm across and 3.193 down. The figure is orthographic and carries real geometry, so every front position below is a measurement rather than a fraction. THE FIRST READING OF THE SAME FIGURE WAS WRONG AND IS RECORDED SO IT IS NOT REPEATED: a page rule three pixels below the panel put the detected height at 303 px and the aspect at 4.60, which reads exactly like a schematic figure that may not be measured at all.","lifecycle":"searched 2026-08-28, 'UfiSpace S9600-28DX end of life' - no announcement of any kind; the product page and datasheet are live and the unit is actively marketed. none-announced is a real finding, not an omission.","mgmt-block":"figure-measured, jack by jack at 22x. TOD is a full-size RJ45 whose bezel measures 15.33 x 13.16 at (23.46-38.78, 26.94-40.09), keyway DOWN, labelled TOD above. The USB 3.0 socket is MOUNTED ON ITS SIDE - the blue insert is a 1.3 x 9.4 mm vertical bar at (46.9-48.2, 29.1-38.5) inside a 5.3 x 13.4 receptacle - so std/usb-a is placed with rotate: 90 and its `at` recomputed from the landed centre (47.05, 33.05), which is the trap the skill records against the MX204's USB. Below them the RESET button (centre 31.28, 46.51) and, along the bottom, the micro-USB console (18.9-26.4, 70.2-73.0), the RJ45 console (bezel centre 37.69, 66.40, keyway DOWN, labelled IOIOI) and the RJ45 management jack (bezel centre 57.71, 66.56, keyway DOWN, green lamps at its two BOTTOM corners, labelled with a network icon). Both consoles reach the same CLI: 'The console can be connected either with the IOIO port or the micro USB port', the micro-USB needing a CP210x driver.","part-numbers":"none stated - neither the datasheet nor the HIG prints an orderable chassis SKU. The accessory lists name only the FRUs (PSU-132-DESR, PSU-132-AESR, FAN-803816-HI), which are the modules' own part numbers and live on their contracts. No SKU is invented here.","port-lamp-bands":"figure-measured - a continuous PCB lamp strip runs above the upper QSFP28 band (y 6.89-14.72) and below the lower one (y 71.9-79.24), each carrying two rows of four-lamp clusters, one row per port: ufispace/lane-led-quad, whose 14.4 mm width matches the measured 14.5 mm four-dot span to 0.7%. THE STRIP IS COLOUR-CODED AND THE COLOURS MEAN SOMETHING: it is yellow from x 53.8 (over the SFP28 block) to 110.4, with its lower half orange from 86.6, and dark green from 110.4 to 214.9. The yellow and orange run covers exactly the SFP28 block and the first QSFP28 column - which is port 0, the 100G port those four SFP28 breakout ports share. The vendor is marking the shared group on the metal. Sampled RGB: yellow 233/216/60, orange 218/108/48, green PCB about 70/95/58.","power":"datasheet for typical, HIG for maximum, and the HIG's maximum is unusually well qualified. Datasheet Environmental: 'Typical power: 324 Watts (no transceiver)' - scope stated. HIG Connecting Power: 894 W maximum on the DC version and 890 W on the AC version, each with an explicit note - 'Testing criteria for maximum power are as follows: Temperature 45 C, Optics: full populated, Traffic: 100% load' - so power-envelope is fully-configured rather than unstated, which is the first device in this vendor set that can honestly say so. The two maxima are 4 W apart and are two measurements of two different builds, not a conflict; the DC figure is carried as the higher and both are named in attrs. PSU inputs from the datasheet (AC 100-240 V 12 A, DC -40 to -75 V 40 A) with the HIG's fuse ratings.","psu-airflow-variant":"THE PART NUMBERS DO NOT MATCH THE CONTRACTS AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. This chassis orders PSU-132-DESR and PSU-132-AESR, both 'exhaust air flow'; ufispace/psu-132-dc and psu-132-ac were drawn for the S9300-32D, which orders the intake-flow PSU-132-DISB1 / AISB1 of the same 1300 W family, and their contracts carry those model strings and airflow. The face is the same 50.5 x 40 module with the same red latch, square vent grid, cord inlet and lamp, so the components are reused and both `model` and `airflow` are overridden per configuration. See the psu-variant-attrs gap: the override makes this device right and leaves the contracts' own attrs saying intake, which is correct for the part they were drawn from.","qsfp28-block":"figure-measured, and this is the layout that has to be got right or the numbering is nonsense. Six columns on a 19.9 mm pitch (three abutting shells of two columns each, measured 91.95-131.68, 131.99-171.71 and 172.02-211.43, i.e. 39.72, 39.72 and 39.41 mm wide) and FOUR rows in two bands: an upper band y 14.41-40.40 and a lower band y 45.73-71.41, each holding two cage rows about a bright white centre bar (26.94-28.50 and 58.26-59.82). Cage faces measure 11.9 mm tall on a 13.46 mm row pitch, which is the same row pitch ufispace/s9321-64e measured on its own 2RU front. NUMBERING RUNS DOWN EACH COLUMN, not along the rows: column k holds 4k in the upper band's top row, 4k+1 in its bottom row, 4k+2 in the lower band's top row and 4k+3 in its bottom row, so the leftmost column is 0/1/2/3 and the rightmost 20/21/22/23. Read off the HIG's own overlay digits, which print 0 4 8 12 16 20 across the first row and 1 5 9 13 17 21 across the second. The top row of each band is mirrored (rotate: 180) - the cage gaskets of both rows face the centre bar.","qsfpdd-block":"figure-measured - the four 400G cages are a 2 x 2 block at x 216.3-256.0, y 29.44-55.44, sitting between the two QSFP28 bands rather than in either of them and to their right. Columns at 217.3 and 237.0 (a 19.7 mm pitch), rows about the centre bar at 41.66-42.91 on the same 13.46 mm pitch as the QSFP28 rows. Numbering runs down the columns again: 24 over 25, 26 over 27. Immediately to their left a blue light-pipe strip carries the port lamps, drawn with ufispace/qsfpdd-led-strip-2x4 - one strip per cage row, each standing beside the two same-row ports, which is the arrangement that component was built for on the S9300-32D.","rear":"figure-measured - four fan bays on an 84.1 mm pitch, the pitch taken from the four status lamps (colour-detected at x 19.1, 103.15, 187.25, 271.35) and confirmed by the bay seams at 6.3, 90.4, 174.5, 258.5 and 342.6. The 80 mm module sits right-aligned in its 84.1 mm slot, giving bay origins 10.2, 94.3, 178.4 and 262.5. The two PSUs are stacked at the right, their origins derived from their own lamps (383.0, 9.3) and (383.0, 51.8) against ufispace/psu-132-ac's status-led at [8.7, 4.3]: x 372.8, y 3.5 and 46.0, a 42.5 mm pitch. THE FACE EDGES GIVE 4.3 AND 45.4 INSTEAD, a 41.1 mm pitch, so the two readings differ by about 1 mm; the midpoint (y 4.0 and 45.7) is carried and the disagreement recorded here rather than hidden. Between the fans and the PSUs sit the grounding pad (a silver plate at x 347.3-357.9, y 6.6-31.9, which the HIG says ships 'covered with a protective label'), the earth symbol beside it, and the FAN 0|1|2|3 legend naming all four bays.","rear-figure-scale":"drawing - HIG Figure 7 (fig-0014) draws the rear 1312 x 264 px for the same 436 x 87.7 mm: aspect 4.9697 against 4.9715, 0.04% out, 3.009 / 3.010 px/mm. Also orthographic, so the rear positions below are measurements too.","sfp28-block":"figure-measured - the four breakout ports are one 2 x 2 ganged block in a white shell at x 51.2-86.0, y 14.09-39.78. Column centres 60.1 and 77.2 (a 17.1 mm pitch, wider than the 14.25 mm std/sfp-ganged part, so the cages sit centred in their columns with a visible wall between them); row centres 20.49 and 33.39 about the shell centre 26.94, a 12.9 mm pitch. Bottom row mirrored. NUMBERING IS 0/1 0/3 ON TOP AND 0/2 0/4 BELOW - it runs down the columns, read off the yellow band's own tiny legends rather than off the HIG's large overlay digits, and the HIG port table confirms only the range '0/1 ~ 0/4'. These four are not extra ports: the datasheet calls them '4 x 1/10/25G SFP28 (In-band port share with 100GE Port 0)'.","sides":"HIG text, positioned by estimate. Section 5 states the mounting explicitly: 'The chassis has 5 attachment pins on each side, for a total of 10 pins', engaging key-shaped holes in the slide rails, plus one M4 screw per side locking the inner rail. Five pin heads and one screw are therefore drawn per flank - the count and the kind are sourced, the spacing is not. AXIS: on a RIGHT view x = 0 is the FRONT and on a LEFT view x = 0 is the REAR (viewer3d.js convention), so the two lists run in opposite directions; both faces here are symmetric front-to-back, which is stated so that the axis is on record as checked rather than as happening not to matter.","sources":"datasheet (s9600-28dx-datasheet, converted) and the Hardware Installation Guide (s9600-28dx-hig, converted, Figures 1-35), plus three vendor images: s9600-28dx-2-front.png, -3-rear.png and -1-angle.png. THE TWO GUIDE ELEVATIONS ARE THE BEST GEOMETRY IN THIS VENDOR'S INTAKE and are what this model is measured from; the photographs were used only to confirm colour and counts.","status-leds":"figure-measured - six lamps in one column at x 10.95-14.39, colour-detected centres y 58.26 to 70.63 on a 2.474 mm pitch, with the sixth lamp drawn BLUE where the other five are green: that is the ID beacon, and it is why the colour detection had to include blue as well as green or the column would have read as five. Labels are printed dark on a white strip to their LEFT (x 5.94-11.26, y 56.38-72.35), reading SYNC SYS FAN PS0 PS1 ID top to bottom - the same six and the same order as the HIG's Front Panel LED table. DRAWN AT A 2.7 mm PITCH, NOT THE MEASURED 2.474: common/led-rect is 2.6 mm tall and cannot sit on a 2.474 pitch without overlapping its neighbour (L13), so the column is stretched 1.13 mm overall and re-centred on the measured centre 64.45. Same compromise, same reason, as ufispace/m3000-14xc and ufispace/s9501-28smt record.","timing-block":"figure-measured - three jacks in one column at x centre 13.0, each labelled ABOVE its own jack rather than below (the S9501-28SMT prints its labels beneath): 1PPS SMB centre y 7.99, 10MHZ SMB centre y 22.40, GNSS ANT SMA centre y 36.65. Drawn circles 7.2, 7.2 and 9.4 mm across - the SMA reads larger than the two SMBs, which is the correct relationship - but the outlines drawn are common/smb-jack and common/sma-jack's own contract sizes, not these numbers. THERE IS NO BITS JACK on this device: the datasheet's timing list is GNSS, 10MHz, 1PPS and ToD only, and the faceplate carries no fifth timing connector. Its cell-site siblings all have one, so its absence is stated rather than left to be noticed.","top":"drawing-fraction - the HIG Figure 4 top view is dimensioned (W 436, D 762) but its own drawn aspect is 0.527 against a true 0.572, 8% out, so it does NOT pass Gate 1 and only fractions are taken from it. Seven shallow full-width channels were edge-detected down the lid, spanning x 14.3-422.9, at depths 121-139, 218-236, 314-332, 411-429, 507-525, 604-622 and 683-701 mm as fractions of the drawn depth. AXIS: y = 0 is the REAR, per the house top-view convention.","vent-islands":"derived - a vent field is a perforation and the drawing said so, but the marks printed inside one were floating on air (L64). The vendor interrupts the perforation where it prints, so each of those marks now has a solid patch under it in the chassis colour, drawn over the vent the way ufispace/s9600-72xc paints its port bands over one. The patch is the printing's own footprint plus 0.4 mm, which is what the S9610-36D's front render measures: its slots stop 0.4 mm outside each lamp cluster and resume 0.4 mm past it. Where a vent is simply measured wider than the metal it reaches, this states the metal that the printing proves is there without re-measuring the field.","vents":"figure-measured extent, SIMPLIFIED SHAPE. The faceplate is a square-perforation field over most of its area, and the perforated region was measured by dark-run scanning per row band (top strip y 0.6-6.3 from x 16 to 435; bottom strip y 79.3-87 full width; the whole right-hand block x 256-435 between them; the band between the two QSFP28 rows x 0.6-216 at y 40.7-45.4; and patches around the left-hand connectors). circle.data-description: HIG Fan FRU LED table - Off (no input power), Green (fan FRU function normal), Amber (fan FRU abnormal, service is required). Three rows, no blink states: this table is shorter than the S9510-28DC family's and is transcribed as it stands rather than filled out from a sibling

circle.data-description: HIG PSU FRU LED table - Off (no input power to all power supplies), Green (output on and OK), Blinking Green (standby state / only +5VSB on, or firmware updating), Red (critical event causing shutdown - failure, over current, short circuit, over voltage, fan failure, over temperature), Blinking Red (input power lost with a second supply in parallel still powered), Blinking between Green and Red (warning event, supply continues to operate - high temp, high power, high current, slow fan)

g.data-description: the designated grounding location of HIG section 8 - two tapped M4 holes on the rear, between the fans and the PSUs, shipped covered with a protective label that is removed before the accessory lug (29 x 37.5 x 12.5 mm, #6 AWG) is bolted on. Measured off HIG Figure 7 at x 347.3-357.9, y 6.6-31.9
